sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Easton, PA?
sections.html:
Yes. An Easton owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it stands. Which route fits depends on the condition of the house, whether anyone is renting it, and how soon you need to close.

Easton is the county seat of Northampton County and the easternmost city in the Lehigh Valley, built where the Lehigh River runs into the Delaware. It sits about 14 miles northeast of Allentown and 51 miles north of Philadelphia, and the Delaware is its eastern boundary with Phillipsburg, New Jersey. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place or an inherited title is where an as-is sale most often comes up in a city this size.

sections.h2: What is Easton like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Easton is compact and dense. Census QuickFacts lists 4.26 square miles of land and 6,597.9 residents per square mile in 2020, so most blocks sit close to the next. The city is split into four districts: Downtown, College Hill, South Side and West Ward.

Downtown is low ground at the river junction, ringed by hills to the north, west and south. College Hill, just north, is the home of Lafayette College. South Easton lies across the Lehigh and was a separate borough until 1898. A buyer will weigh these points about your block:

  • Roads: US 22 (the Lehigh Valley Thruway) crosses central Easton, PA 611 follows the Delaware, and PA 248 starts where those two meet. Interstate 78 clips the southeast corner, with its nearest interchange in Williams Township.
  • The river crossings: the Northampton Street Bridge and the Easton and Phillipsburg Toll Bridge link the city to New Jersey.
  • Downtown draws: Centre Square, the Crayola Experience and the National Canal Museum bring visitors into the core.
  • Winters: Easton averages roughly 30 inches of snow, sits in hardiness zone 6b, and has recorded a low of minus 15 degrees Fahrenheit, so roof, gutter and pipe condition get questions.
  • Schools: Easton Area School District serves the city along with Forks and Palmer townships, with Easton Area High School in Palmer Township.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Easton homes?
sections.html:
Easton's median owner-occupied home was valued at $196,300 for 2020 to 2024, and just 44.5% of homes are owner-occupied, so renters shape much of the market. The estimated population reached 30,402 in July 2025, which is 8.2% above the 2020 estimates base.

A median is a midpoint, so a renovated Downtown house and an unrenovated College Hill one can land far from it. Use recent sales on your own street, not the citywide figure, to judge an offer.

sections.h2: Which Easton rules should I check before selling?
sections.html:
Check the city's code office first, then the historic district rules, then rental paperwork if a tenant lives in the house. Easton's Code Enforcement department applies the city Property Maintenance Code and the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, and it also answers questions about open permits.

  • Permits: building, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, or changing its use, calls for a permit, as does new electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing work.
  • Historic district: facade or signage work can also need a certificate of appropriateness from the Historic District Commission.
  • Occupancy: no more than three unrelated people may live together as one housekeeping unit, and an Occupancy Limitations Certificate states the maximum for each dwelling unit.
  • Rentals: an owner who rents must file each tenant's name and address with the Rental Licensing Officer, and the city tracks move-ins through a moving permit from the Finance Department.
  • Fire safety: the city fire inspector will do a free fire safety inspection if you doubt a building has the required smoke detectors.

If a tenant lives in the house, collect the lease, the rental license papers and the tenant form before you list, since a buyer will ask for them.

sections.h2: How do Easton property taxes and transfer costs work?
sections.html:
Two bills fall on an Easton house: the city levies 24.95 mills on the value set by the Northampton County Assessment Office, and the county and school district send their own. The city also collects an earned income tax of 1.45%, which becomes 1.95% with the Easton Area School District's 0.5%.

Northampton County mailed its 2026 bills in mid-January, with a discount through March 31 and the face amount due June 1. Unpaid county taxes go to the Tax Claim Bureau at close of business on January 31 of the following year, which was January 31, 2027 for the 2026 bill. Pay or settle any balance at closing so the buyer starts clean.

The state realty transfer tax is 1% of the value, and Pennsylvania holds both the person handing over the deed and the person receiving it liable. The Recorder of Deeds, reachable at (610) 829-6210, collects it along with any local tax when the deed is recorded, and the city lists a real estate transfer tax among the taxes it levies. Ask the Recorder for the combined rate on your price before you sign.

If you think the assessment is too high, the county's 2026 appeal hearings ran from August 5 to October 29. Ask the Assessment Division, on the second floor of the courthouse at 669 Washington Street, for the current filing deadline. A homestead exclusion, set up under Act 72 of 2004, lowers the school tax base on an owner's primary home, and an owner-occupant selling should confirm with the district what happens to the exclusion at transfer.

sections.h2: What does Pennsylvania require from an Easton seller?
sections.html:
A seller of one to four dwelling units must give the buyer a signed, dated property disclosure statement before the two of them sign the sales agreement. That duty comes from 68 Pa.C.S. section 7303. The form asks about the roof, basement, pests, structure, plumbing, heating, electrical, soils and drainage, hazardous substances, and legal issues touching title.

A seller who willfully or negligently breaks the rule answers for the buyer's actual damages, and a suit has to begin within two years after final settlement (section 7311). Fiduciaries who sell to administer a decedent's estate are outside the disclosure chapter (section 7302). These duties apply to a cash buyer's purchase the same way they apply to a listing.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Easton?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time, condition or occupancy rules out a normal listing. Typical Easton situations include:

  • An inherited house nobody plans to live in.
  • A tenant-occupied house where the rental paperwork or the unit itself needs work.
  • Open permits or code notices that would slow a lender-financed buyer.
  • Heavy repairs after a harsh winter, such as roof, plumbing or heating failures.
  • A move date set by a job, a divorce or a court calendar.

Compare any cash figure with what a listing would net after repairs, concessions and transfer tax. If you want a number for an Easton address, call or text and describe the house, including any tenants or open code items.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale of an Easton house take?
faqs.a: It depends on title work and the closing date you agree to, and a cash buyer does not wait on a lender's underwriting. The deed still has to be recorded with the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds, and any unpaid taxes or liens are cleared from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer tax on an Easton sale?
faqs.a: The sales agreement sets the split. Under state law both the person giving the deed and the person receiving it are liable for the 1% state tax, and the Recorder of Deeds collects any local share with it.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Easton house with a tenant still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Easton requires owners who rent to keep the tenant's name and address on file with the Rental Licensing Officer, so hand the buyer the lease, the rental license papers and that tenant form.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a house in Easton?
faqs.a: The Northampton County Recorder of Deeds records it. That office files deeds and mortgages and collects the fees and taxes due on property transfers, and its phone number is (610) 829-6210.

faqs.q: What if I inherited the Easton house?
faqs.a: You can still sell it. Pennsylvania exempts property passed by will or by intestate succession from realty transfer tax, and a fiduciary selling for an estate is outside the seller disclosure chapter. Settle title with the estate's attorney before the closing date.
